summary: Verified on HEAD 2f082fd40. Originality, legal and sensitivity stays at 8.0 and is ON PAR: the score is at least 7.5, no blocker is open, and no major is open. I reproduced the reviewer's one major (O2-1) but downgraded it to a minor. The RIFT clock numbers are real: content/modes.json:18-19, :31-40, :46, :51-52. They are also missing from _harness/probe_sim_rekey.ts: I counted 57 rows and none covers RIFT's start, bounty, waves or ranks. But ruling 4's binding gate covers the W4 systems re-key. Its text says 'Rows W4 adds after this date fall under the same gate', and the RIFT clock was never a W4 row. That clock is a recorded research decision (DESIGN_NOTE.md:61, from r02), and game rules are not protected assets. So no gated row is breached, which is what kept the first review's C1 at major. One correction: FRAY's 1,400 has no ARAM counterpart, because FRAY is a free-for-all. BRIDGE is the ARAM analogue, and its start is gated. All four minors were reproduced. names_check: 'Summoners Rift' comes back clean, while the apostrophe and plural forms hit, and with no arguments the CLI prints 'clean (0 strings checked as name)' and exits 0. secret_scan PASS (903 files). A git grep run from the repo root for the vendor-key pattern finds 10 files on master f800a9fef and origin/master 09720db0b, and 0 on HEAD. Note that a git grep run from games/vale finds 0 on master, because it only searches that subtree. The Dunsom mask crop shows a cracked gold mask with dark eye recesses. It reads a little skull-like at chip size but not as horror, so it stays a minor. I found no missed blocker.

The gate holds 57 rows: spells, starters, boots, wards, buffs, the BRIDGE and Quick starts, the Wick bounties and passive Gleam. It has no RIFT start, kill bounty, wave cadence or rank rows, while content/modes.json gives 480/280/18/[6,11,16]/30-30-90. Those rows sit outside ruling 4's W4 scope, so this is an honesty gap rather than a gate breach (O2-1, now a minor). FRAY's 1,400 is not an ARAM counterpart.

findings.title: RIFT's match clock sits on LoL's numbers and rules, and the re-key gate never checks it
findings.what: RIFT starts with 480 Gleam (LoL 500, -4 %) and a kill pays 280 (LoL 300, -6.7 %). The assist share of 50 %, the level cap of 18, the 5 basic ranks and the ult ranks at 6/11/16 match LoL. So do waves at 0:30 then every 30 s, upgrades every 90 s, the 3+3 composition with a big unit every 3rd wave, and surrender at 4 of 5. None of these is a probe_sim_rekey row.
findings.evidence: content/modes.json:18-19, :31-40, :46, :51, :52 (BRIDGE also :108 ranks). The row list of _harness/probe_sim_rekey.ts has 57 rows and no RIFT start, bounty, wave or rank rows (grep sys:/what:). _harness/_reports/closing_originality2_ungated_numbers.txt. _design/DESIGN_NOTE.md:61 records the clock as the r02 decision.
findings.fix: Optional backlog. Re-key the RIFT clock off LoL: for example, start Gleam of 420 or less, a kill bounty of 240 or less, waves at 0:20 then every 25 s (Quick already does this), a different ult cadence or level cap. Then add the rows to probe_sim_rekey.ts and re-soak pace to 22-28 min. FRAY needs no change.
findings.verifierNote: I reproduced every number. I downgraded the severity from major to minor. Ruling 4's gate is scoped to the W4 systems re-key: 'Rows W4 adds after this date fall under the same gate'. The RIFT clock is a documented r02 design decision outside it, so no binding gated row is breached. That breach is the basis on which the first verifier kept C1 at major. Wave and level cadence are genre-level, non-protectable rules, with no asset copied. Gauge correction: FRAY is a free-for-all, not ARAM. BRIDGE is the ARAM analogue, and its 1,400-start row is gated, so FRAY's 1,400 is not a ruling-4 counterpart. The near-LoL start and kill numbers are still an honest originality gap, and the backlog should log it.

findings.title: Dunsom's cracked-gold mask reads skull-adjacent at chip size
findings.what: Dark eye recesses and a crackle pattern on the gold mask. It is not a horror read.
findings.evidence: _harness/_shots/closing_originality2_dunsom_face.png, viewed by me. Cracked gold mask, dark recesses, wide flat hat, rounded cowl.
findings.fix: At the next Dunsom pass, put lit dawnglass in the eye recesses, merge the crackle into broad planes, and carve a calm mouth line. Then re-run the facechip gate.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed visually. Not horror, not a hockey mask, not a blank mannequin, so it stays a minor.

findings.title: names_check misses an apostrophe-less possessive, and with no arguments it prints a misleading 'clean'
findings.what: 'Summoners Rift' passes the lint, while the apostrophe and plural forms hit. Run with no arguments, the CLI prints 'clean (0 strings checked as name)' and exits 0.
findings.evidence: `node tools/names_check.ts "Summoners Rift"` gives clean (1 string checked). The forms "Summoner's Rift" and "Doran's Blades" give HIT. Run with no arguments, the CLI prints clean (0 strings) and exits 0.
findings.fix: Emit the variant that keeps the bare 's' on non-final words. With no arguments, scan the full catalog or exit 2 with a usage message.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced. No real string in the catalog leaks this way.

findings.title: master and origin/master still hold the vendor-key literal in 10 pipeline scripts
findings.what: HEAD is clean, but the default branch tip still carries the literal until this branch merges.
findings.evidence: Run from the repo root, git grep for the meshy-api-key rule pattern (tools/secret_scan.ts:29) finds 10 files on master f800a9fef, 10 on origin/master 09720db0b and 0 on HEAD. They include pipeline/colosseum_meshy_meshes.py, colosseum_meshy_remesh.py and meshy_anims.py. No key was printed.
findings.fix: Merge or cherry-pick the env-read change to master, and run `npm run secrets` on master.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced. Running git grep from games/vale gives a false 0 because the search is limited to that path.
